newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says no reason for further shift to VAT.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says no reason for further shift to VAT.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said he saw no reason why he would switch the tax burden further on to VAT (indirect tax) if his Conservative Party stays in power after the May 1 election.

"I have no reason to suppose that we are going to continue to make a switch towards value-added tax, but I make that point on the basis that we are going to keep public expenditure down and we don't see any need to," he told reporters at a news conference.
The ruling Conservatives have cut the standard rate of income tax by two pence since 1992, but have increased the rate of VAT and extended the list of goods on which VAT is charged.
"I do not foresee a direct switch from income tax to value added tax because I do not think we will have to raise extra taxes," he added
